testimonials.author: Ms. Zhang
testimonials.body: Our concierge Xiao Zhou was incredibly attentive — she sent all the pre-trip notes to our group chat and reminded us of the day's plan and weather every morning. Our local guide Ah-Ming really knew the geology of Zhangjiajie and even wove Tujia folk tales into our walk through Jinbianxi — our kids were mesmerized. The best part was not having to plan anything ourselves; Haitao handled everything.

testimonials.author: M53****383
testimonials.body: Took my parents to Yunnan. The VIP fast-track access genuinely saved hours of queueing. Our driver was steady and punctual across every leg — Kunming, Dali, Lijiang. Hotels were all five-star group properties; my parents especially loved the one in Lijiang overlooking Jade Dragon Snow Mountain. Meals were well-curated too, with Cross-bridge rice noodles and a mushroom feast.

testimonials.author: Ms. Lin
testimonials.body: I was worried solo travel would be lonely, but concierge Xiao Zhao tailored my Guilin-to-Yangshuo itinerary to my pace and even rearranged a couple of stops. My Li River cruise had a window seat with a great breeze. The in-house driver knew the local roads well and dodged several traffic snarls. Zero-shopping tours like this are a godsend for solo travelers.

testimonials.author: Mrs. Wang
testimonials.body: Third time booking with Haitao — this one was a five-day Wulong Three Natural Bridges plus Xiannu Mountain tour in Chongqing. Same as before: zero shopping stops, zero hidden fees, fully transparent contract pricing. We ran into our guide Tao-zi again — old friends by now! Her stories about Ciqikou were even more vivid this time. Highly recommend for anyone tired of being scammed.

We maintain deep partnerships with leading travel platforms including Ctrip, Facebook, and Google. Our team includes over 500 employees, with 270 senior multilingual professional guides, and we welcome more than 100,000 travelers every year. After years of growth, we have built a highly capable operations team and a comprehensive after-sales service system. Quality without compromise and shopping-free tours are our promise; bringing travel back to its purest form is our mission. Beyond traditional group tours, our group operates 113 luxury hotels and 27 high-end boutique guesthouses. We also offer full-service travel planning covering itineraries, hotels, local transportation, attraction tickets, and bundled bookings — all tailored to your needs. Unlike standard group tours or independent travel, we craft flexible journeys around your schedule and interests, ensuring a worry-free and secure experience from start to finish.

chongqing.title: Chongqing Travel
chongqing.overview: Chongqing — a magical city where mountains meet rivers and cultures intertwine. Marvel at the mighty Yangtze, soak up the charm of this mountain city, savor authentic hotpot, and immerse yourself in the unique Bayu culture. From the dazzling lights of Hongyadong to the vibrant buzz of Jiefangbei and the timeless lanes of Ciqikou, every corner enchants. Whether it's your first visit or a deep second go, you'll find a travel rhythm that suits you perfectly.

1.title: Hongyadong
1.subtitle: Every step reveals a new view; savor the beauty shaped by time.
1.description: The soulful haven of old Chongqing — you won't know its dreamlike magic until you visit. Step inside and you travel through time, enveloped by centuries of history. Stroll by the river and the grandeur of Hongyadong meets the rushing Yangtze — a view beyond words.
notes: If you're short on time, skip going inside Hongyadong.
Best viewing time: visit Hongyadong between 19:00 and 23:00 for the night view.
Nearby sights: Qiansimen Bridge is right beside Hongyadong, and Jiefangbei is just a short walk away.
1.closing: Hongyadong blends Bayu culture, magical scenery and everyday local life. Plan wisely to skip the crowds and soak up the full charm of this mountain city.

2.title: Mount Fairy (Xiannu Mountain)
2.subtitle: Stroll through and feel as if you've stepped into a fairyland, embraced by nature's gentle calm.
2.description: A dreamy destination that steals your heart! Every step is a romantic encounter with nature — scenery so poetic it makes you forget the world. Mountain breezes brush your face, green fills your eyes, and summer feels like heaven. Meadows, forests, peaks — every corner hides a secret of nature, waiting to be explored.
notes: Avoid the crowds: 10:00-12:00 on public holidays is the peak entry period.
Mount Fairy has an annual average temperature of just 18°C. Bring a light jacket in summer and a down coat in winter.
Pair it with Wulong Tiankeng (Three Natural Bridges) for a one-day tour.
2.closing: As the sunset drapes Mount Fairy in golden silk and the forest whispers fade into birdsong, the day becomes more than a feast for the eyes — it becomes a healing for the soul.

3.title: Three Natural Bridges
3.subtitle: A geological marvel: decoding the timeless beauty of the Three Natural Bridges.
3.description: A World Natural Heritage site and filming location for Transformers: Age of Extinction, these three natural stone bridges — formed hundreds of millions of years ago — are nothing short of a geological wonder. Stand beneath Tianlong Bridge and gaze up at its 235-meter span, or wander through the shadowy caverns of Heilong Bridge listening to the Pearl Spring's tinkling drops. The awe is hard to put into words.
notes: Wear comfortable shoes — there's a lot of walking in the scenic area.
On sunny days, shooting against the light reveals more layered, translucent textures of the water surface.
Can be combined with Mount Fairy on the same day.
3.closing: Remember — slow down and feel with your heart, and the true awe and wonder of the Three Natural Bridges will unfold. It's the perfect destination for a relaxed sightseeing experience.

4.title: Chiyou Jiuli City
4.subtitle: The largest Miao village in Chongqing, featuring traditional Miao culture on a grand scale — truly one of a kind.
4.description: The most complete window into Miao culture in Chongqing, with over 40 traditional buildings hiding thousand-year codes of wood carving, costume, and bamboo-pole dance. The only place in China that honors Chiyou — one of the "Three Ancestors of Huaxia" — and recreates the migration history of the Jiuli tribe. A spiritual landmark of Miao cultural identity.
notes: The park is large — allow at least half a day.
The Nine Gates, Jiuli Palace, and Jiuli Divine Pillar are all Guinness World Records-holding structures.
Folk experiences include door-blocking wine, flowing-water banquets, and bonfire nights — all free in the nighttime open area.
4.closing: If you want to add a cultural touch to your Chongqing itinerary, Chiyou Jiuli City is a worthwhile stop — highly rated by older travelers and families.

5.title: Wu River Gallery
5.subtitle: Falling for the grandeur of mountains and rivers, while cherishing the quiet of old-town lanes.
5.description: 江水如翡翠般碧綠，在煙波浩渺中畫舫尋幽，纔是真正的“人在畫中游”。高山深谷、峽灩相接，飛瀑流泉、古樹蒼藤，構成了令人驚歎的自然奇觀。
notes: Wear non-slip sports shoes — paths get slippery after rain.
Temperatures on the river shift a lot — bring a windproof jacket. During the rainy season, check live navigation notices from the scenic area.
When exploring old towns, wear comfortable shoes so you can stroll the flagstone lanes with ease.
5.closing: Slow down — when the morning mist's fishing lights and the evening boat songs become your memory landmarks, the soul of the Wu River quietly finds its way into your heart.

sichuan.title: Sichuan Tours
sichuan.overview: Sichuan Province, abbreviated as "Chuan" or "Shu," covers 486,000 square kilometers and is China's fifth-largest province. Its terrain is varied, with significant east-west differences — high in the west, low in the east — encompassing mountains, hills, plains, basins, and plateaus. The Sichuan Basin is one of China's four great basins and home to rich historical and cultural treasures including Jiuzhaigou, Huanglong, Dujiangyan, Mount Qingcheng, Leshan Giant Buddha, and Mount Emei. Sichuan is also a vibrant multi-ethnic family, hosting China's second-largest Tibetan area, the largest Yi area, and the country's only Qiang autonomous county — with colorful ethnic festivals held throughout the year.

1.title: Jiuzhaigou Scenic Area
1.subtitle: Spring sunshine and blooming romance; summer greens and refreshing cool of Jiuzhaigou.
1.description: Jiuzhaigou is a forested mountain valley named for the nine Tibetan villages nestled among its alpine lake clusters. A World Natural Heritage site and National AAAAA Scenic Area, Jiuzhaigou is celebrated for its "Six Wonders" — alpine lake clusters, waterfalls, colorful forests, snow-capped peaks, blue ice, and Tibetan culture — earning it the title "King of Waterscapes."
notes: Autumn brings the richest color play between forest and lakes. If time allows, reserve a full day for an in-depth visit — combining walking with sightseeing buses gives the most complete experience.

2.title: Bipenggou Scenic Area
2.subtitle: A paradise for hiking enthusiasts and one of China's most celebrated spots for autumn foliage
2.description: 東連臥龍自然保護區，南接四姑娘山風景區；與四姑娘山、臥龍共同構成「大熊貓走廊世界遺產地」。景區擁有自然景點82個，象璀璨的珍珠般鑲嵌在畢棚溝的六個分景區內。是一個集原生態景觀博覽、登山穿越、極地探險、滑雪滑冰、休閑度假於一體的大型原生態旅遊風景區。
notes: Autumn foliage season and the first snowfall are peak times — book tickets and transport in advance, and bring wind- and cold-proof gear suited to the weather.

3.title: Huanglong Scenic Area
3.subtitle: Vividly colorful travertine pools and rare karst landforms
3.description: China's only well-preserved highland wetland, renowned worldwide for its "Four Wonders" — colorful pools, snow-capped mountains, deep gorges, and ancient forests. The travertine pools shift through a rainbow of hues as the surrounding scenery and angle of sunlight change, earning it the nickname "Fairy Pool on Earth." Huanglong is celebrated for its grand scale, ingenious structure, and vividly colored surface travertine landscape, as well as its rare karst formations known across the world.
notes: Huanglong sits at a relatively high elevation — take it slow, stay hydrated, and aim for around midday on clear days when the colors of the pools are at their most brilliant.

4.title: Mount Siguniang Scenic Area
4.subtitle: High-altitude snow peaks known as the "Chinese Alps" — a paradise for hiking enthusiasts
4.description: Mount Siguniang is the highest peak of the Qionglai Range on the eastern edge of the Hengduan Mountains, made up of four continuous snow-capped summits that stand like four maidens draped in white veils, rising one after another above the two silver rivers of Changping Valley and Haizi Valley. It has long been a hiker's paradise — the gorge trails are rugged and narrow, with meltwater from the snow peaks trickling gently down in streams; over the ridges lie broad alpine meadows carpeted in wildflowers, painting scenes of gentle, exquisite beauty.
notes: First-time visitors should start with the easy-to-walk Shuangqiao Valley sightseeing route, which packs plenty of scenery in for moderate effort. Serious trekkers can then add a deeper route into Changping Valley.

5.title: Ruoergai Re'er Grassland
5.subtitle: China's second-largest grassland, after the Hulunbuir Grassland
5.description: Re'er Grassland is China's second-largest grassland, second only to the Hulunbuir Grassland, and is home to the famous natural wetland Flower Lake. The grassland is dotted with lakes and grazed by cattle and sheep; along the way, Tibetan-style homestays run by herdsmen offer food and horse-riding. The best time to visit is July and August in summer, when the hillsides burst into bloom with wildflowers.
notes: Pair this stop with the First Bend of the Yellow River's Nine Curves — the evening light against the grassland horizon is incredibly photogenic, so time your visit for sunset.

zhangjiajie.title: Zhangjiajie Tours
zhangjiajie.overview: The core scenic area of Zhangjiajie is the Wulingyuan Scenic Area — when people talk about traveling to Zhangjiajie, they usually mean Wulingyuan. Wulingyuan Scenic Area is made up of Zhangjiajie National Forest Park, Tianzi Mountain Nature Reserve, Suoxiyu Nature Reserve, and Yangjiajie Nature Reserve. Other famous city attractions include Tianmen Mountain National Forest Park, where the heart-stopping glass skywalks and the magical, dreamlike Tianmen Cave are always visitor favorites, hailed as the "new legend of Zhangjiajie". Not far from the city, the "Best Cave Mansion in China" — Huanglong Cave — and the "Fairy Pool on Earth" Baofeng Lake can be reached by bus or taxi. On the city's edge, the "Hundred-Li Gallery" Maoyan River rafting, Sangzhi County's "Asia's No. 1 Cave" Jiutian Cave, Furong Town, and the "World's No. 1 Rafting" Mengdong River rafting are all wonderful places for sightseeing.

1.title: Zhangjiajie National Forest Park
1.subtitle: China's first national forest park — a "miniature fairyland and an enlarged bonsai"
1.description: Divided into sub-areas including Huangshizhai, Pipaxi, Jinbianxi, Yaozizhai, Shudaogou, and Yuanjiajie, it is the essential core of any Zhangjiajie trip. Geologically in the youthful stage of peak-forest evolution, the landforms are strikingly unusual: stone pillars stand densely packed in endlessly varied forms, vegetation is lush, the slopes are steep, the ravines are deep, and the climate is warm and humid. Huangshizhai is the most celebrated section inside Zhangjiajie National Forest Park — there is a saying that goes "You haven't truly visited Zhangjiajie unless you've been to Huangshizhai."
notes: Enter early and start with the Yuanjiajie and Jinbianxi main trails, then, depending on your energy, add Tianzi Mountain or Yangjiajie — it saves time and helps you skip the busiest crowds.

2.title: Tianmen Mountain National Forest Park
2.subtitle: High-altitude peak, sheer cliffs, glass skywalks — a true masterpiece of nature
2.description: Tianmen Mountain takes its name from the natural wonder "Heaven's Gate Cave." As you ride the cable car up, the scenery of the mountain below unfolds beneath your feet. The centerpiece is Tianmen Mountain Temple. The glass skywalks, built along sheer cliffs, are an absolute must — gazing down into the sheer, bottomless valleys while walking through the air delivers a thrilling, once-in-a-lifetime rush. Tianmen Mountain offers three classic sightseeing routes, each with its own iconic highlights.
notes: Plan a combined route linking the cable car, the glass skywalk, and Tianmen Cave — and aim your photo stops for morning or late afternoon, when drifting mist adds beautiful depth to the mountains.

3.title: Tianzi Mountain
3.subtitle: Four iconic wonders — sea of clouds, moonlight, glowing sunset skies, and winter snow
3.description: Located in the north of Zhangjiajie National Forest Park and bordered by the Suoxiyu scenic area to the east, Tianzi Mountain takes its name from the early-Ming Tujia leader Xiang Dakun, who styled himself "King Xiang, Son of Heaven." Its highest point reaches about 1,262.5 meters and its lowest about 534 meters, and visitors here can witness the four signature wonders — drifting clouds, moonlit nights, sunset-tinged skies, and winter snow. Hundreds of millions of years ago, Tianzi Mountain lay beneath a vast ocean; through long and complex geological processes it rose into the strange and iconic landforms you see today, including the celebrated Yubi (Imperial Brush) Peak.
notes: On clear days, spend extra time at the main viewing platforms. If you're lucky enough to catch a sea-of-clouds day, the peak-forest scenery here is breathtaking — and incredibly photogenic.

4.title: Zhangjiajie Huanglong Cave
4.subtitle: China's only cave you can tour at night, packed with countless stalactites and stalagmites
4.description: Huanglong Cave is famous for its soaring cavern ceilings, deep underground rivers, and dense forest of stalagmites. The cave rises to over 100 meters at its highest point — and the entire cave system contains caves within caves and rivers running through it. Its signature sight is the "Dinghai Shenzhen" (Pillar that Calms the Seas), a stalagmite that has been growing for 200,000 years and rises 20 meters tall — yet only 10 centimeters wide at its narrowest — so valuable that the park has insured it for 100 million yuan. The cave offers both a walking route and a boat ride, so visitors can explore it on land and water.
notes: Experience in this order: walk through the cave first, then take the underground river boat — a more comfortable pace that lets you fully appreciate the cave lighting and karst details.

5.title: Zhangjiajie Grand Canyon
5.subtitle: Stand on the Grand Canyon Glass Bridge for a sweeping view of the gorge far below
5.description: A natural museum of Zhangjiajie's landscape in miniature — mountains, water, and caves all in one place — where visitors can admire the full sweep of northern-temperate karst scenery in a single trip. The canyon is thick with lush vegetation and fresh air, with cascading waterfalls and bubbling streams around nearly every turn — a true natural oxygen bar. Beyond the breathtaking scenery, the park's must-try highlight is the world's tallest and longest glass bridge. Standing on the Zhangjiajie Grand Canyon Glass Bridge, you gaze straight down at the canyon floor 400 meters below.
notes: Book a glass-bridge time slot in advance and leave plenty of time for queuing and walking. Photographers will enjoy the bridge most during off-peak hours.

guangxi.title: Guangxi Tours
guangxi.overview: Guangxi is a hidden realm where majestic mountains and rivers meet the warmth of everyday life. Half of it is poetic, picture-perfect nature, and the other half is the lively bustle of local streets — together they weave a travel experience unlike any other. In Guangxi, every corner is a landscape painting: emerald hills and clear waters, where you become a brushstroke wandering the scene. Nanning's Qingxiu Mountain fills your heart with green, every breath scented with the freshness of leaves and grass. Liuzhou's luosifen is a riot of bold, spicy flavor. Guilin's mountains and rivers are like the fine brushwork of a Song-dynasty poem — beautiful beyond words.

1.title: Guilin
1.subtitle: "Best under heaven" — the moment you speak those words, you know you've truly arrived in Guilin
1.description: “桂林山水甲天下，陽朔山水甲桂林”是對這片土地最精準的概括。漓江是廣西的精華與靈魂，清澈的江水纏繞着青黛色的喀斯特峰林，構成一幅流動的天然畫卷!
notes: Must-see attractions: the Li River, Elephant Trunk Hill, Yangshuo West Street, the Longji Rice Terraces, and the Two Rivers and Four Lakes.
Spring (March-May) and autumn (September-November) are the best times to visit Guilin.
Guilin's weather is changeable, so be sure to check the forecast in advance and choose a fine day for your visit.
1.closing: Make time for a trip to Guilin: feel the breeze along the Li River, wander through Xingping Ancient Town, visit the Yangshuo viewpoint pictured on the RMB 20 note, and discover why Guilin's scenery is celebrated as the finest under heaven.

2.title: Beihai
2.subtitle: A small coastal city “named for the sea and born alongside it”
2.description: Beihai is a travel gem many people overlook, yet once there, you may “never want to leave.” Its charm lies not in being “dazzling,” but in feeling “comfortable”—a place where body and mind unwind and life returns to its simple, authentic rhythm.
notes: Snap up Weizhou Island ferry tickets 15 days in advance; Silver Beach is quietest for sunrise at 6 a.m.
Try beachcombing at low tide (catching fish and shrimp and collecting seashells, usually starting after 5 p.m.).
2.closing: Silver Beach shimmers like a river of stars, Weizhou Island tells a thousand-year love story between sea and volcano, and the lively old street intertwines with sunrise over the water to create the most soothing romance.

3.title: Nanning
3.subtitle: Half the warmth of everyday life , half a poetic dreamscape
3.description: Nanning seamlessly blends natural beauty, deep history, and vibrant local life. Here, verdant hills and graceful rivers meet timeworn lanes and bustling night markets.
notes: Nanning is hot and humid, so sun protection + an umbrella are essential.
The sights are spread out, so do not overpack your day; exploring at an easy pace is far more enjoyable.
Slurp down a bowl of Laoyou rice noodles, then browse a night market—that is the perfect way to experience Yong City.
3.closing: With an open, welcoming spirit, Nanning weaves together beautiful landscapes, rich history, and the pleasures of everyday life, inviting travelers to savor them at leisure.

4.title: Liuzhou
4.subtitle: A distinctive city where landscapes intertwine with industry, and everyday life coexists with poetry
4.description: Its appeal reaches far beyond a bowl of fragrant, spicy luosifen. It also lies in the sweeping Liu River scenery, where “the winding water twists like nine coils,” the citywide bloom of spring bauhinias, and a deep historical legacy enriched by vibrant ethnic traditions.
notes: At Liuhou Park, dance with the breeze, climb among the greenery, and savor nature's beauty to the fullest.
At the Liuzhou Industrial Museum, trace the marks of years gone by and reflect on the passage of time.
A bowl of luosifen, two braised eggs, and a few good friends—memories of Liuzhou are simple and beautiful.
4.closing: With clear waters, green hills, and delightful scenery, this place is praised as “the world's largest natural bonsai.” Here, you can immerse yourself in vibrant ethnic traditions, taste authentic local food, admire the landscapes, and encounter beauty when you least expect it.

5.title: Chongzuo
5.subtitle: A city that honors culture and courtesy, the capital of sugar, cradle of the ancient Luoyue, where poetry and wine compose a splendid chapter
5.description: This border city does not rely on grand plazas, bustling shopping districts, or trendy photo-stop gimmicks. What truly captures the heart is the natural stillness of its mountains and waters. The scenery waiting around each corner feels like secret savings tucked in your pocket—reassuring, dependable, and entirely your own.
notes: Detian's drifting spray, Mingshi's rice fields, and Huashan's rock paintings are all verses Chongzuo has written for the world.
The border area is regulated. Avoid photographing military personnel, police, or guard posts, and follow staff instructions rather than taking unnecessary risks.
Paths are slippery in the rainy season, so wear non-slip shoes. A raincoat is more practical than an umbrella and leaves your hands free to hold the railings.
5.closing: Here, you can experience nature's distinctive allure. Whether it is the spectacular Detian Transnational Waterfall or the serene beauty of the Mingshi countryside, each will make you want to linger. Every landscape has a character of its own, filling your journey with wonder and moving moments.

guizhou.title: Guizhou Tours
guizhou.overview: Guizhou is a hidden realm where wondrous mountains and waters blend seamlessly with vibrant ethnic traditions. Half is nature on a majestic scale, half a richly colored cultural tapestry, together creating a travel experience both distinctive and captivating. In Guizhou, every frame looks like a perfect wallpaper: among mighty peaks and graceful waters, I become a dot of ink roaming through the painting～At Huangguoshu in Anshun, cool spray brushes the face while the thunderous roar fills the ears with grandeur. At Libo Xiaoqikong, emerald pools gleam like jade, and a boat ride feels like drifting through a painting. At Fanjing Mountain in Tongren, a solitary peak pierces the clouds; only from the summit does the vastness of heaven and earth unfold. At Xijiang Miao Village in southeastern Guizhou, thousands of lights shine like stars, creating the warmest human scene after nightfall. Across the Chishui Danxia landforms in Zunyi, red cliffs and cascading waterfalls reflect one another, and walking through them feels like crossing into the Jurassic age.

1.title: Huangguoshu Waterfall
1.subtitle: Spring torrents and summer cascades rise in mist; autumn runs clear and winter freezes into an otherworldly realm
1.description: Huangguoshu Waterfall is China's largest waterfall and one of the world's most famous, named after the Chinese banyan trees widespread in the area. It is a national AAAAA-rated tourist attraction and appears on the tentative list for World Natural Heritage status. Its mighty flow, six-direction viewing spectacle, shifting scenes inside and outside Water Curtain Cave, and karst gorge scenery are known collectively as the 「Four Wonders of Huangguoshu」, earning it the title 「China's Premier Waterfall」.
notes: During the high-water season (June-August), the flow is at its most powerful and spectacular. Visit in the morning for favorable light, then combine Tianxing Bridge and Doupotang into a one-day highlights itinerary. Bring a raincoat for walking through Water Curtain Cave.

2.title: Libo Xiaoqikong
2.subtitle: Spring pools glow emerald and summer forests invite exploration; autumn mist veils the bridge and winter waters mirror the sky
2.description: Libo Xiaoqikong is a karst wonder centered on an ancient seven-arch bridge, named after a Qing-dynasty stone bridge spanning the Xiangshui River. It is a national AAAAA-rated tourist attraction and a key part of the 「South China Karst」 World Natural Heritage Site. Its emerald waters and secluded pools, tiered cascades, water forest, limestone caves and underground rivers, and Buyi culture are collectively known as the 「Five Charms of Xiaoqikong」, earning it the title 「Emerald on the Earth's Belt」.
notes: Water is abundant in summer, making the water forest perfect for the refreshing experience of 「walking through cascades and splashing in the stream」. Enter early to avoid peak tour-group crowds, and alternate between walking and sightseeing shuttles for a more relaxing visit.

3.title: Fanjing Mountain
3.subtitle: Spring clouds billow, summer greenery glistens; autumn skies soar crisp and clear, while winter snow drapes the mountain in gauze
3.description: 梵淨山是武陵山脈主峰，因「梵天淨土」的佛教寓意而得名。世界自然遺產，國家AAAAA級旅遊景區，中國五大佛教名山之一。以紅雲金頂的險峻、蘑菇石的奇絕、雲海佛光的變幻以及黔金絲猴的珍稀並稱「梵淨四奇」，被譽為「天空之城」。
notes: Spring and autumn have the most stable weather with high probability of sea of clouds. Climbing Red Cloud Golden Summit requires using chain handrails — wear non-slip shoes and check weather alerts. Tickets must be reserved in advance on the official platform.

4.title: Xijiang Miao Village
4.subtitle: Spring terraces gleam green, summer nights glow with fireflies, autumn harvests ripple in gold, winter fires reflect on towers.
4.description: 西江千戶苗寨是全世界最大的苗族聚居村寨，因上千座吊腳樓層層疊疊分佈於兩座山巒之上而得名。國家AAAA級旅遊景區，中國歷史文化名鎮。以萬家燈火的夜景、苗族吊腳樓建築群、高山流水敬酒禮、銀飾刺繡工藝和苗族飛歌古歌並稱「西江五韻」，被譽為「中國苗都」。
notes: Ascend the viewing platform at dusk to capture the magical moment when sunset glow meets the first evening lights. We recommend staying overnight for an immersive Miao village experience—morning mists swirling through the village creates an even more serene atmosphere than the night scenery.

5.title: Chishui Danxia Tourist Area
5.subtitle: Spring bamboo drips emerald, summer waterfalls bring coolness; autumn forests blaze with color, winter mist veils everything.
5.description: Chishui Danxia is one of China's largest Danxia landform areas — named for its red sandstone cliffs contrasting with green bamboo and waterfalls. Part of the UNESCO China Danxia site. Known for Danxia cliffs, waterfalls, bamboo forests, cycad fossils, and red culture.
notes: Summer is the best season for Chishui Waterfall and Foguang Rock — wear non-slip sandals for water access. The three scenic sections are far apart, so driving or chartering is best. Reserve a full day.

yunnan.title: Yunnan Tour
yunnan.overview: South of the Clouds — Yunnan. Here lies Shangri-La from Hilton's novel, the paradiseRock saw, and the sacred Meili Snow Mountain. Flowers bloom year-round amid ever-changing scenery. Kunming, the spring-like capital; Lijiang's ancient town; Dali's romance; Xishuangbanna's tropical charm; and Diqing (Shangri-La) — a pilgrimage site and trekking paradise.

1.title: Erhai Lake
1.subtitle: By Cangshan Mountain and Erhai Lake, amid wind, flowers, snow and moon
1.description: One of Dali's four famous 'Wind, Flowers, Snow, Moon' scenery spots, Erhai Lake is ear-shaped, formed by the collapse of the Western Erhai River. Known as the 'Flawless Jade Among Mountains,' it features three islands, four islets, five lakes, and nine winding bends with crystal-clear waters. Popular lakeside villages include Shuanglang with its 'Divine Light of Erhai,' Caicun where the film 'Blueless' was shot, and Xizhou, renowned for its Bai ethnic architecture.
notes: Cycle around Erhai or take a leisurely charter to connect Shuanglang, Xizhou, and Caicun — experience lake views, local culture, and regional cuisine all in one day.

2.title: Lugu Lake Scenic Area
2.subtitle: Highland lake scenery and Mosuo matriarchal culture
2.description: Straddling Sichuan and Yunnan provinces, Lugu Lake is home to the Mosuo, Yi and Pumi peoples. Its clear blue waters make it Yunnan's highest-altitude lake and one of China's deepest freshwater lakes, shrouded in mystery. Surrounded by towering mountains with snow cover for over three months each year and rich forest resources, it is dubbed a "fairyland on earth." Highlights include the Goddess Cable Car, Small Grassland Sea and the Three Islands of Lugu — electric buggy lake tours are the most popular way to explore.
notes: Stay at a lakeside inn — morning mist on the lake and evening sunset are Lugu Lake's most atmospheric moments.

3.title: Lijiang Ancient Town
3.subtitle: Wooden buildings with grey tiles — look up and see Jade Dragon Snow Mountain
3.description: One of the most famous towns on the Ancient Tea Horse Road with 800-900 years of history. Wooden buildings with grey tiles, stone lanes, bridges over streams — look up from East Street and see Jade Dragon Snow Mountain. One of two ancient towns in China successfully inscribed as UNESCO World Heritage sites in their entirety.
notes: Explore the ancient alleys and Mu Mansion by day, then enjoy the city lights and local music by night for a complete experience.

4.title: Jade Dragon Snow Mountain
4.subtitle: The closest snow mountains to the equator — the southernmost snow mountains in the Northern Hemisphere
4.description: The sacred mountain of the Naxi people — Shanzidou's main peak at 5,596m, perpetually shrouded in mist, an unconquered virgin peak. The 12 snow peaks feature glaciers, alpine meadows, and pristine forests. Rhododendrons bloom at different altitudes with the seasons.
notes: At high altitudes, acclimatize gradually following park guidance. Pair with lower-altitude spots like Blue Moon Valley for a more comfortable itinerary.

5.title: Shuhe Ancient Town
5.subtitle: Compared to Lijiang, it is even more tranquil here
5.description: Shuhe Ancient Town lies northwest of Lijiang, nestled by mountains and water — quieter than Dayan. Backed by the Jade Dragon Snow Mountain foothills, it features well-preserved stone bridges and temples. Part of the Lijiang UNESCO World Heritage site.
notes: If you prefer a quiet slow-travel pace, Shuhe is better for a longer stay than Dayan — more relaxed for coffee, photos, and strolls.

beijing.title: Beijing Tours
beijing.overview: Beijing — a magnificent city blending millennia of imperial grandeur with modern style. Half golden-tiled royal splendor, half hutong alley life. Every step echoes history: the Forbidden City, the Great Wall, Temple of Heaven, Summer Palace, Tiananmen Square — each telling stories of China's glorious civilization.

1.title: The Palace Museum
1.subtitle: Crimson walls, golden tiles — a thousand years in a glance
1.description: The Forbidden City — the imperial palace of the Ming and Qing dynasties — is the world's largest and best-preserved ancient wooden architectural complex. A UNESCO World Heritage site housing over a million cultural relics. Stroll along the central axis from the Meridian Gate to the Gate of Divine Prowess and feel the weight of 600 years of history.
notes: Allow at least half a day to stroll along the central axis from the Meridian Gate to the Gate of Divine Prowess.
Forbidden City tickets must be reserved in advance through official channels — no on-site sales.
Avoid weekends and holiday peaks — weekday mornings have fewer visitors.

2.title: Badaling Great Wall
2.subtitle: A mighty dragon coiling the mountains, standing guard in the north
2.description: The Badaling section is the best-preserved and most iconic portion of the Ming Great Wall, and the first to open to visitors — hailed as one of the Nine Great Passes of China. A World Heritage Site and national 5A scenic area, it features steep terrain, towering walls, and densely placed watchtowers with distinct scenery across all four seasons. Take the cable car up, then hike to North Four Tower or Hero Peak for sweeping views of the dragon winding through the peaks.
notes: Take the cable car up, then hike to the North Fourth Tower or Hero Slope.
Avoid weekends and holidays — early morning or late afternoon have fewer crowds.
Temperature varies greatly on the mountain — bring a light jacket in spring and autumn.

3.title: Temple of Heaven
3.subtitle: Round heaven, square earth — quietly praying for a bountiful year
3.description: The Temple of Heaven was where Ming and Qing emperors offered sacrifices for good harvests — the largest ancient sacrificial complex in China. A UNESCO site featuring the Hall of Prayer, Echo Wall, and Circular Mound Altar. Visit in the morning to see locals exercising.
notes: Visit in the morning to avoid crowds and experience local life.
The Hall of Prayer for Good Harvests, Echo Wall, and Circular Mound Altar are must-sees.
The park is large — allow 2-3 hours for your visit.

4.title: Summer Palace
4.subtitle: Lakes and hills mirror each other — an imperial painting come to life
4.description: The Summer Palace — built during the Qianlong and Guangxu reigns — is China's largest and best-preserved imperial garden, centered on Kunming Lake and Longevity Hill with Jiangnan-style landscaping. A UNESCO site featuring the Tower of Buddhist Incense, the Long Corridor, and the Seventeen-Arch Bridge.
notes: Beautiful year-round, especially in spring and autumn.
Take a boat across Kunming Lake for a different perspective.
Large grounds — allow half a day for a leisurely visit.

5.title: Tiananmen Square
5.subtitle: Heart of the nation, where all hearts converge
5.description: Tiananmen Square lies on Beijing's central axis and is the largest city square in the world, serving as an important national symbol and venue for political activities. At its center stands the Monument to the People's Heroes, the solemn Tiananmen gate tower rises at the northern end, the National Museum of China is on the east side, and the Great Hall of the People is on the west. The daily flag-raising ceremony is solemn and dignified, drawing countless people who wait through the night. You can combine your visit with the National Museum, experiencing the continuity and glory of Chinese civilization between history and the present.
notes: The daily flag-raising ceremony time varies with sunrise — check in advance and arrive early.
Combine with the National Museum of China — free entry but advance reservation required.
Security check required to enter the square — please carry ID.

xian.title: Xi'an Tours
xian.overview: Xi'an — a legendary ancient capital with a thousand years of history. Touch Qin bricks and Han tiles, hear Silk Road camel bells, taste rich lamb soup, immerse in the epic of thirteen dynasties. From the Terracotta Warriors to the ancient city wall, Big Wild Goose Pagoda to Tang Paradise, every corner tells the story of Chang'an.

1.title: Emperor Qinshihuang Terracotta Warriors Museum
1.subtitle: A "terracotta army" that stunned the world — the pinnacle of Qin-dynasty military art.
1.description: Recognized as the Eighth Wonder of the World, the site has unearthed thousands of life-sized terracotta warriors and horses, each face uniquely distinct, arranged in formidable formations with overwhelming grandeur, vividly recreating the fierce armies and royal processions of the great Qin Empire more than two thousand years ago. The scale of the pit ruins is colossal and the level of detail breathtaking — an essential destination for anyone seeking to experience the spirit of China's first unified dynasty.
notes: The Terracotta Army is located in Lintong District, about a one-hour drive from central Xi'an. It is recommended to set aside at least half a day for this visit. Be sure to follow a guided tour or use an audio guide during your visit — otherwise you risk seeing only the clay figures without grasping the historical context.

2.title: Xi'an City Wall
2.subtitle: China's best-preserved and largest ancient city wall
2.description: This Ming Dynasty city wall encircles the ancient center for 13.7km — its broad top is perfect for walking, cycling, or taking an electric car. Battlements, watchtowers, and barbicans remain well-preserved. Standing on the wall, you see ancient streets inside and modern skyscrapers outside — a striking contrast of past and present.
notes: Best to ascend at dusk to enjoy both sunset glow and city lights. Cycling on the wall is popular but the brick surface is uneven — be careful. The South Gate (Yongning Gate) section has the most brilliant night views.

3.title: Big Wild Goose Pagoda & Square
3.subtitle: Where the Tang monk Xuanzang translated scriptures — the most romantic Tang cultural landmark
3.description: Big Wild Goose Pagoda is a square brick pagoda housing rare Buddhist relics. Climb for panoramic southern views. The north square hosts Asia's largest musical fountain; the south square is perfect for photos. The whole area blends ancient charm with lively leisure.
notes: The fountain show runs at a fixed time every evening — arrive early to grab a spot. The free viewing terrace on the 3rd floor of Joy City, by the south square, is the best angle to photograph the pagoda's full silhouette.

4.title: Tang Paradise
4.subtitle: A Tang Dynasty-style pedestrian street ablaze with lights and bustling crowds
4.description: Running north to south, this Tang-inspired district becomes a dazzling spectacle after dark, as red lanterns, Tang-style architecture and monumental sculptures unfold one after another—as though the world of The Longest Day in Chang’an had been brought to life. Free street performances include the roly-poly dancer, a levitating Terracotta Warrior and Li Bai poetry challenges, while shops on both sides sell Tang-style hanfu, creative cultural gifts and intangible-heritage snacks. Whether you come to watch, take photographs or immerse yourself in a journey back through time, the experience is immensely rewarding.
notes: Go after 19:30 when the lights are fully on for the best experience. To interact and take photos with the roly-poly performers, check the schedule on the official platform and queue up. Weekends are extremely crowded — mind your belongings.

5.title: Shaanxi History Museum
5.subtitle: An underground treasury of Chinese civilization — a hall distilling 3,000 years of dynastic history
5.description: This national museum houses 370,000+ artifacts spanning from prehistoric pottery to Shang-Zhou bronzes, Han tiles, Tang gold and silverware, and murals. The agate cup with gold animal head and the silver pot with dancing horse are world-famous national treasures. Walking through the time-ordered halls is like reading a three-dimensional history of ancient China.
notes: Free entry but requires real-name reservation days in advance via the official Shaanxi History Museum WeChat account. ID required for entry. The densely packed exhibits merit an audio guide or tour guide — otherwise easy to skim. Allow at least 2.5 hours.
